If the display becomes empty, immediately skip every remaining eligible player.** Finish the display step by **discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three: prestige faceup, blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card**. ### II. Family (Rules pp13–14)

Starting with the Chairman title holder, clockwise, each player resolves their family action:

1. Check where your opportunity marker was **at phase start** (it begins off the board).
2. Choose a main family action: take it once, or **may take it twice if the marker already matched it**.
3. **Place/move the opportunity marker onto your chosen main action.**
4. After the main action, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant its extra action. This extra action is never doubled by the marker and never moves the marker.

If placing a family piece with none in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize's printed VP. This applies to firm-share creation too. If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.

| Family action | Effect |
|---|---|
| Enlist Writer | Place a member in any Presidency's Writers box. With at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer **once this turn**, so a doubled Writer action can place three total. |
| Enlist Officer | Place a member in Officers-in-Training. |
| Purchase Luxury | Pay bank £4; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned, and its window icon; social enterprise. |
| Purchase Shipyard | Pay bank £2; take shipyard and place its matching ship **unfitted on that shipyard**, not in a sea zone. Shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. |
| Purchase Workshop | Pay bank £5; take workshop; manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus; worth 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. |
| Seek Share | Place a member on an empty Stock Exchange space and pay bank: the five queue spaces are £2, £3, £3, £4, £5 (two distinct £3 spaces). It is an applicant, not yet a share. |

**New Company shares:** After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both remain. ### III. Hiring (Rules pp14–16)

Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; its owner gets the card. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists, or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

**Own-family hiring needs verbal consent from every other player in that office's candidate pool, EXCEPT that a Chairman election never requires Nepotism consent. Commander appointments are also exempt.**

**Nepotism and its exceptions:**

| Selection | Own-family consent requirement |
|---|---|
| Ordinary office hire | Verbal consent from **every other player represented in that office's candidate pool**. |
| Chairman election, including deadlock fallback | **Exempt from Nepotism**; use the shareholder election/fallback rules. |
| Commander appointment | **Exempt from Nepotism**; use Army piece counts. |

| Office | Hirer and candidates |
|---|---|
| Chairman | Shareholders elect as below. |
| Director of Trade | Chairman chooses current officeholder other than Chairman/Governor; if all offices vacant, any writer. Commanders are not officeholders. |
| Manager of Shipping | Chairman chooses any writer. |
| Military Affairs | Chairman chooses a Presidential Commander; if none, any officer; if none, any Officer-in-Training. |
| President | Director of Trade chooses **a writer OF THIS PRESIDENCY or a Governor ASSOCIATED WITH THIS PRESIDENCY**. |
| Governor | Associated President chooses writer or officer in the region; Commander is not an officer and is ineligible. Place member on Governor overlay. |
| Superintendent of Trade in China | Chairman chooses any writer; office hired immediately upon creation. |
| Governor General | Replaces Director of Trade and is hired the same way. |

**Chairman election:** Former Chairman first announces **the number of shares needed for a pure majority** (more than half of current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one winner's Company shares into Chairman slot and give title marker. It still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms. If no candidate gets support, former Chairman picks any shareholder including self; no Nepotism consent. If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, a prize (lose prize VP). If impossible, there is no Chairman.

Each President chooses order of its Commander, Governors and its own Trade. Must allow each position an opportunity but Commander/Governors may decline. ### Commanders and Deploy (pp22–23)

**At the START of Commander operations, before Deploy attempts**, first request President's treasury funds for any printed-price local alliances in Army; President must approve purchase. Move purchased alliances to the **top/active** half. **When used for Deploy or defense, exhaust the whole alliance to the bottom half.** Its strength is usable once that turn and cannot be split among more than one purpose. **Refresh exhausts any unused active alliances too; it does not reactivate alliances as it does officers/regiments.**

**May Deploy repeatedly while able, including after a success: there is no one-success-per-turn cap.**

1. Target own Presidency's home, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region. Cannot target another home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. Company region must have unrest or a closed order to give action an effect.
2. Exhaust chosen officers/regiments to bottom for one die each and local alliances for printed dice. Subtract the combined strength of target and **all other regions in its empire, counting target only once**. Company-controlled defense strength is zero. Roll normal check; a noncatastrophic failure can retry using remaining resources.
3. After **each attempt**, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in attempt; each 6 returns an officer to supply. Regiments never roll officer losses.

On success, take loot from the bank: **£4 per target tower + faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of (surviving officers used in this attempt + 1)**. The extra £1 guarantees the Commander's minimum share even if no officers survive. Count only this attempt's surviving participating officers and used regiments/alliances.

| Each payout cycle | Pay in this order, stopping when cash runs out |
|---|---|
| Commander family first | £1 for Commander **plus £1 for each of their used surviving officers**. |
| Other families clockwise | £1 per used surviving officer of that family. |
| Bank last | £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance **piece**, regardless of strength. |

**Repeat that entire cycle from the Commander until all loot is distributed.** The Commander also receives one trophy per target tower.

**After loot and trophies, impose successful control in this order:**

| Step / piece | Action and destination |
|---|---|
| 1. Political strength | Remove target tower and dome. If target was an empire capital, remove **every matching empire flag throughout India**. |
| 2. Orders and unrest | Open **all** target orders and remove **all** its unrest. |
| 3a. Loot/control token, on a new conquest | Turn it region-symbol side up and put it **ABOVE THE ASSOCIATED PRESIDENT'S BOX**. |
| 3b. Governor overlay, on a new conquest | Put it **IN THE CONQUERED REGION ON THE MAP**. |
| 3c. Governor office card, on a new conquest | Put **only the CARD** in **Vacant Offices**, awaiting later Hiring. |
| 4. Elephant | If it faced outward from the conquered region, move it **fully inside that region**, now threatening Rebellion. |

Steps 3a–3c form a new Governorship only if the target was not already Company-controlled. **With Governor General in play, no new Governor or Governor overlay is created; printed Company symbols indicate control.**

**Deploying in an already Company-controlled region to reopen orders or clear unrest:** Company defense penalty is zero; no tower remains, so gain **zero tower trophies**. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, use the **minimum loot of surviving participating officers + 1 for the Commander**, distributing normally.

On catastrophe, Commander returns half own family's trophies rounded up and Commander member to supply. Exhausted officers still check losses. Commander has no office card to vacate.

### VI. Revenue (p27; firms pp41–42)

If deregulated, firms pay expenses/dividends first. Then Company:

1. **Expenses:** Reduce Balance £1 per existing Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones, including China. Exclude Commanders. If insufficient, take £5 emergency loans. After using emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower Standing two.
2. **Expectations:** Compare remaining Balance to the expectations under **current** Standing; if lower, lower Standing one.
3. **Dividends:** Chairman may pay any affordable number. Each dividend costs one cash per Company share; pay each owner £1 per share, including Chairman. **Company shareholders cannot waive payment.** If total cash paid as dividends is **strictly greater** than expectations, advance Standing one space.

Standing reaching leftmost space means Company failure. During Revenue, go immediately to Final Scoring.

### VII. Events in India (pp28–33)

**First roll the storm die:** a sea-zone result affects **that zone**, three storms affects **ALL sea zones**, and no storm indication means **NO storm checks**. The die face also specifies the **number of India events**. Resolve all required storms **before drawing any event**. Then flip and resolve **one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as the number printed on that die face**. Where an event uses a region, normally read the **back of the new top tile** in the draw stack, not the tile just drawn; follow each event's specific location rule.

**Storms:** Determine eligibility in the zone(s) specified above before rolling:

| Ships | Storm exposure |
|---|---|
| Company and extra ships | **Exempt**; never roll storm checks. |
| Player-owned ships in Company fleets | Check ships in the affected sea zone(s). |
| Ships assigned to China | Count as **Eastern** sea zone. |
| Firm ships | Count in the sea zone on their **firm strategy**, even though on a charter. |

| Step | Procedure |

| 4. Court/workshops | Score Company shares and, on failure, uninvested workshops, as below. |

|---|---|
| Survived | Roll office attrition, then retire Pensioners; **no prestige/display cards**. |
| Failed | Instead draw **ONE RANDOM Company failure card** and resolve its printed consequence. |

### I. London Season (Rules pp11–12)

**Attrition:** Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. **Retirements:** Starting with the Chairman (former Chairman if vacant), clockwise, each player may retire each pensioner to a prize. **Prestige:** Players who completed at least one pensioner retirement **or an eligible firm special retirement during this London Season** must each take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties: most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. Acting player may peek at display blackmails. **Do not replace a chosen/discarded card during selection. If the display becomes empty, immediately skip every remaining eligible player.** Finish the display step by **discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three: prestige faceup, blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card**. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.

Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Make required enterprise/share trades immediately upon taking the spouse. ### II. Family (Rules pp13–14)

Starting with the Chairman title holder, clockwise, each player resolves their family action:

1. Check where your opportunity marker was **at phase start** (it begins off the board).
2. Choose a main family action: take it once, or **may take it twice if the marker already matched it**.
3. **Place/move the opportunity marker onto your chosen main action.**
4. After the main action, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant its extra action. This extra action is never doubled by the marker and never moves the marker.

If placing a family piece with none in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize's printed VP. This applies to firm-share creation too. If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.

| Family action | Effect |
|---|---|
| Enlist Writer | Place a member in any Presidency's Writers box. With at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer **once this turn**, so a doubled Writer action can place three total. |
| Enlist Officer | Place a member in Officers-in-Training. |
| Purchase Luxury | Pay bank £4; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned, and its window icon; social enterprise. |
| Purchase Shipyard | Pay bank £2; take shipyard and place its matching ship **unfitted on that shipyard**, not in a sea zone. Shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. |
| Purchase Workshop | Pay bank £5; take workshop; manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus; worth 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. |
| Seek Share | Place a member on an empty Stock Exchange space and pay bank: the five queue spaces are £2, £3, £3, £4, £5 (two distinct £3 spaces). It is an applicant, not yet a share. |

**New Company shares:** After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both remain. ### III. Hiring (Rules pp14–16)

Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; its owner gets the card. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists, or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

**Own-family hiring needs verbal consent from every other player in that office's candidate pool, EXCEPT that a Chairman election never requires Nepotism consent. Commander appointments are also exempt.**

**Nepotism and its exceptions:**

| Selection | Own-family consent requirement |
|---|---|
| Ordinary office hire | Verbal consent from **every other player represented in that office's candidate pool**. |
| Chairman election, including deadlock fallback | **Exempt from Nepotism**; use the shareholder election/fallback rules. |
| Commander appointment | **Exempt from Nepotism**; use Army piece counts. |

| Office | Hirer and candidates |
|---|---|
| Chairman | Shareholders elect as below. |
| Director of Trade | Chairman chooses current officeholder other than Chairman/Governor; if all offices vacant, any writer. Commanders are not officeholders. |
| Manager of Shipping | Chairman chooses any writer. |
| Military Affairs | Chairman chooses a Presidential Commander; if none, any officer; if none, any Officer-in-Training. |
| President | Director of Trade chooses **a writer OF THIS PRESIDENCY or a Governor ASSOCIATED WITH THIS PRESIDENCY**. |
| Governor | Associated President chooses writer or officer in the region; Commander is not an officer and is ineligible. Place member on Governor overlay. |
| Superintendent of Trade in China | Chairman chooses any writer; office hired immediately upon creation. |
| Governor General | Replaces Director of Trade and is hired the same way. |

**Chairman election:** Former Chairman first announces **the number of shares needed for a pure majority** (more than half of current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one winner's Company shares into Chairman slot and give title marker. It still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms. If no candidate gets support, former Chairman picks any shareholder including self; no Nepotism consent. If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, a prize (lose prize VP). If impossible, there is no Chairman.

### Presidency operations and Trade (pp20–21)

Each President chooses order of its Commander, Governors and its own Trade. Must allow each position an opportunity but Commander/Governors may decline. No President may fill another President's home region, even if its office vacant. Increase Balance by each order's printed value, **or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn under Deregulation**. ### VII. Events in India (pp28–33)

**First roll the storm die:** a sea-zone result affects **that zone**, three storms affects **ALL sea zones**, and no storm indication means **NO storm checks**. The die face also specifies the **number of India events**. Resolve all required storms **before drawing any event**. Then flip and resolve **one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as the number printed on that die face**. Where an event uses a region, normally read the **back of the new top tile** in the draw stack, not the tile just drawn; follow each event's specific location rule.

**Storms:** Determine eligibility in the zone(s) specified above before rolling:

| Ships | Storm exposure |
|---|---|
| Company and extra ships | **Exempt**; never roll storm checks. |
| Player-owned ships in Company fleets | Check ships in the affected sea zone(s). |
| Ships assigned to China | Count as **Eastern** sea zone. |
| Firm ships | Count in the sea zone on their **firm strategy**, even though on a charter. |
| Hobnob firm ships | **Exempt** from storms. |

Roll **once per eligible ship**: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Return a sunk ship to its shipyard **unfatigued**.

**Closing orders and Cascades:** Return any writer on a newly closed order to its owner's supply; flip a filled token to closed. If told to close an order in an already fully closed region, Cascade: close all open orders directly connected to that region's orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region's northernmost open order instead. If none are open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate a Cascade only once per event tile but can receive multiple Cascades' effects.

| Event | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Turmoil | Close northernmost open order in top-stack region; if all closed, Cascade. |
| Windfall | Owners take £1 per writer on orders in top-stack region and every bordering region. |
| Shuffle | Elephant's March, then shuffle this tile with remaining draw stack; separately shuffle discards and place on top. If draw stack empty, March last instead. |
| Leader | Top-stack sovereign region gains one tower. Dominated region instead rebels with printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled. |
| Peace | Open orders connected across Elephant's border and add one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant wholly inside a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March. |
| Crisis | Resolve at Elephant's location, tail attacking head, then March. Use procedures below. |
| Foreign Invasion | Roll storm die for target regions: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal; all storms means each, none means top-stack region. Per target roll ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack. On success close all orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target's flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. |

**Choose the ordinary Crisis procedure from the Elephant:** Its **tail is the attacker/acting region; its head is the defender**. A sovereign actor (large capital flag or unflagged dome) causes **Invasion**. A dominated actor (small flag or no dome) causes **Rebellion against its sovereign**. If Elephant is wholly inside a Company region, resolve Rebellion against the Company. This classifier concerns ordinary Elephant-located Crisis events; Foreign Invasion uses its own location rule.

**Invasion Crisis:** Sovereign attacker's whole empire strength + event modifier must be **greater than** defender's whole empire strength. On success, replace defender's flag with attacker's dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its entire empire. If attacker had no empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none available no new empire/flags form. On failure, attacker loses one tower.

**Rebellion Crisis:** Compare only rebelling region strength + modifier against its sovereign capital's strength; other empire regions do not count. Must be strictly greater. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed). Failure removes one tower from the capital.

**Attacks on Company:** An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve attacks in this order: **primary Crisis first**, then secondary regions in **Bombay → Madras → Bengal** Army order. **Within each Presidency, that Commander chooses the order of its associated regions.** Attack strengths are distinct:

- **Primary normal Crisis:** normal Invasion/Rebellion attack strength **plus unrest in its target region**.
- **Primary Foreign Invasion:** the ordinary attack die, with no added unrest (designer ruling in FAQ).
- **Every secondary Rebellion:** **only the number of unrest cubes in that secondary region**; no event modifier or empire strength.

**Mounting defense — first identify who acts:**

| Defense office situation | Acting player |
|---|---|
| Associated Commander occupied | That Commander chooses and exhausts pieces; normal trophy gains/losses apply. |
| Commander vacant | **Military Affairs itself acts in the Commander's stead**, choosing pieces; gains/loses **no trophies**. |
| Commander AND Military Affairs vacant | **Chairman chooses pieces** and gains/loses **no trophies**. |

This is acting for the defense, **not appointing a new Commander**. The acting player exhausts active Army pieces to reach at least the Crisis strength, or as many as possible if unable to reach it. Local alliances provide printed strength usable once; **their strength cannot be split among more than one purpose**. The following strength comparison applies the **user-supplied interpretation** recorded under Special Rules & Edge Cases:

| Total strength of newly exhausted pieces | Attack and defense result |
|---|---|
| **EQUAL TO OR GREATER THAN** Crisis strength | **The attack FAILS; defense SUCCEEDS.** Remove all unrest in the attacked region. The **actual Commander gains one trophy**; **Military Affairs/Chairman substitutes gain OR lose NO trophies**. If this defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible. |
| **LESS THAN** Crisis strength | **The attack SUCCEEDS; defense FAILS.** Perform Region Loss. If the successful primary Crisis was an Invasion, apply empire creation/growth. |

**Example:** Exhausting an active strength-2 local alliance successfully defends a strength-1 Crisis. Exhaust the whole alliance piece; its excess strength does not cause the defense to fail.

**Region Loss:** Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up, then Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in associated Army: each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate Governor: return office card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies. Remove Governor overlay, partially built Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion's specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to its region with **the £ loot side DOWN and the region-symbol side UP**. Future conquest gets no loot modifier; region loses its Presidency association. An Invasion Crisis closes all its orders, or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals number of regions lost **so far this turn**, including this one: first -1, second additional -2, etc. If this causes failure, finish Events in India before Final Scoring. **Losing one region does not automatically lose any other Company region: resolve each other attack and its defense separately.**

**Elephant's March:** After successful Invasion Crisis, move to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise top-stack region. Company region: place fully inside. Dominated region: point toward its sovereign. Sovereign: point across shape-marked border on tile. If that neighbor is already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor that is not. If all neighbors dominated, use the redirect-arrow shape's border, pointing toward empire capital.

<!-- qa-unit:T168:end -->

### VIII. Parliament Meets (pp34–36)

PM must draw at least one law, revealing them one at a time. **After one or two ordinary (non-dilemma) draws, the PM may stop drawing, or continue up to three total. Choose any one law already revealed and discard the others.** Drawing a dilemma instead forces selection of that dilemma and ends drawing immediately. **Before voting**, PM moves the dial's arm clockwise or counterclockwise, stopping on the **first** policy space matching the chosen law's bottom icon. That space fixes the target and consequence. Read law and set Vote marker to its printed starting support.

**Voting:** Starting PM, clockwise, players cast votes; each £1 family cash buys one vote, plus printed card votes. **Each card's votes may be used only once in the entire vote, across all rounds: rotate it when used and leave it rotated until vote resolution. It cannot vote again in a later round of the same vote.** Adjust support up/down; tracks unlimited. PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes must end voting. A player who voted for may later oppose; once opposed, cannot vote for during this vote. Track all opposition votes: biggest opponent holds Opposition Leader; tied current holder retains it. With recipient's consent, votes may be cast on behalf of someone who already opposed or commits to oppose; add them to that person's opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced use of the "Vote with my enterprises" promise.

**Resolution:** -1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma's If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial; new PM moves proposed policy one space either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. Zero or higher passes: place law with passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve selected policy **then** immediate law effects. **Finally restore every card used for voting to its regular orientation**, after either outcome. If law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.

Prestige enterprises count as enterprises of their printed type for these policies.

| Policy | Effect |
|---|---|

Firm managers control firms; firm shares can be traded like Company shares. A firm has two treasuries: **London** receives the bank's £5 per investment and pays for ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses; **India** receives trade and pays dividends/expenses. **Investment cash always comes FROM the BANK TO London. #### Firms phase: investments (pp38–39)

After Family share creation, before Hiring, take investments actions without set order until nobody wishes more. Manager resolves timing conflicts within firm; PM resolves conflicts between firms. Then choose strategies.

- **Form a firm — only if you currently manage none:** return one eligible Company share to supply or flip workshop to invested side. **Flip your family board to its firm-charter side**, then place a family member as first firm share, set value cube to leftmost track space and take £5 from bank into the London treasury.
- **Invest:** With manager's consent, same Company-share/workshop contribution creates one firm share and £5 bank to London. Up to ten firm shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no shares. Cannot use Chairman share. Cannot use Company shares at all when Standing and/or Debt on lined space. Cannot use shares created this turn, even after trading them away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested: no bonus or Company-failure VP; they remain invested even if firm fails.
- **Ships:** A firm may fit a ship from **its own OR ANOTHER PLAYER'S shipyard**, but **must have that shipyard owner's consent**. Pay **£3 FROM the firm's London treasury TO the BANK**. May buy player-owned ship already in Company with owner's consent: unfatigued £3, fatigued £2, paid **from the firm's London treasury into Shipping treasury**. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.
- **Hostile takeover:** Only a player who **manages NO firm at all** may initiate one; managing a different firm also makes you ineligible. Obtain consent of holders of a majority of the target's shares, then move firm's ships, money and shares to own charter, copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.
- **Merger:** Managers negotiate with **every shareholder's consent**. Highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Players may negotiate share transfers. **If the primary would exceed ten shares, RETURN the excess shares to their OWNERS' SUPPLIES, with those owners' consent.** Entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer. Primary's value/dividend track remains the continuing firm's track.
- **Voluntary dissolution:** All shareholders must consent. Apply the same dissolution procedure as an insolvent firm: **shares go to Debtor's Prison (each −1 VP), ships return to their matching shipyards, and the charter flips to its family side. Workshops remain invested for the rest of the game.**

<!-- qa-unit:T376:end -->
<!-- qa-unit:T387:begin -->
#### Firm strategies and competing trade (p40)

After the Firm Investments step ends, managers choose firm strategies.

**Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Only a firm with at least one ship may select a trade strategy; it may select a closed home port.** Managers select their strategy simultaneously and secretly:

| Choice | Eligibility and commitment |
|---|---|
| Trade zone/home port | Commit a secret cash bid from London treasury. The selected home port must be **open when filled**; strategy selection itself does not open it. |
| Hobnob | No bid, trade or dividends. Still pay expenses; retain previous dividend marker for retirement. |

**Reveal cash bids simultaneously, but keep strategy cards facedown until their matching Presidency begins.**

Firm ships face storms in strategy zone; Hobnob exempts them.

At beginning of associated Presidency's operations, before any actions, matching firms reveal strategy and roll one die per committed £1, paying bid to bank. At least one 1/2 permits trade. Firm initiative = ship count minus number of successful dice (1s/2s); can be negative. President's successful Trade creates initiative the same way using Presidency ships. After that success, fill orders lowest initiative first. **The President chooses the order among tied traders; the Company does not automatically go first.** If President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill **after Commander/Governors had chance to act**, Chairman choosing initiative ties.

**Fill only OPEN orders**, as many as possible up to **ships + 1**, starting strategy home port, always tracing through its own filled route back there. **Each firm may fill any particular order only ONCE per turn; it cannot refill its OWN earlier order.** Place filled tokens; revenue goes to India treasury. A firm may refill an order filled by a DIFFERENT firm or the Company this turn; Company may refill firms' orders. A previously filled order pays **half listed revenue, rounded down**, not repeated full value. Advance firm Value one space per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.

<!-- qa-unit:T387:end -->
<!-- qa-unit:T406:begin -->
#### Firm expenses, rescue and dividends (pp41–42)

At start Revenue before Company, firms act in initiative order then other firms; ties by manager's most windows then PM clockwise order. Pay £1 per charter ship **plus higher of share count or firm value**; can use either/both treasuries.

If unable to pay, dissolve unless rescued. Dissolution: shares to Debtor's Prison (each -1 VP), ships back to shipyards, charter back to family side; workshops remain invested. Emergency investments follow the Company-share/workshop eligibility rules under **Firms phase: investments**, even when ten-share cap prevents more shares: pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, lower Value one space per emergency investment. Alternatively make an **emergency negotiated merger with only ONE other firm**. The normal merger procedure still applies, including **every involved shareholder's consent**. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover the endangered firm's unpaid expenses.

After expenses, manager may pay dividends **from India treasury only**. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. **Waiving a dividend requires BOTH the shareholder's choice and the MANAGER'S CONSENT**; shareholder consent alone is insufficient. With that consent, the shareholder may forgo payment for any number of shares on any dividend. Record **total actual cash paid out**, not per-share dividend, with dividend cube on Company Balance track. An active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero; Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India money into London.

|---|---|

including fractional points and Company failure

<!-- qa-unit:T414:begin -->
## Scoring / Victory Conditions

The game ends after scenario's final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Normally failure is immediate; failure during Events finishes that phase, and legislation failure finishes vote before scoring. Once game over, stop negotiations, calling promises and playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use. **During all of Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.**

**Final Scoring order — finish each row before the next:**

| Step | Procedure |
|---|---|
| 1. Firms, if deregulated | **BEFORE ordinary Power/Court/final-outcome scoring**, for each player separately add VP from all their shares across all their firms, then **round that player's total DOWN once**. Deduct **1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison**. **The next row (step2) describes the ONE eligible special firm retirement per shareholder, even on Company failure; ordinary scoring begins at step3.** |
| 2. Firm special retirement, if deregulated | Each eligible shareholder may retire **one member from supply**, after firm scoring but **BEFORE Power or any other ordinary final scoring**. Applies whether Company survived OR failed; no display cards. |
| 3. Power | Calculate Power and award its VP, as below. |
| 4. Court/workshops | Score Company shares and, on failure, uninvested workshops, as below. |
| 5. Final retirements OR failure card | Resolve the appropriate Company outcome below. Firm special retirement in step2 occurs in **either** outcome and is not replaced by the failure card. |

**Power award:** Count **enterprises and Company shares**, using their current Power-track rates (bottom two positions zero), +1 per passed-law token and trophy, +2 for PM, plus printed card power (blackmail faceup or down, applicable spouse). Most/second awards are **3/1 VP if final turn 1–3, 5/2 if turn 4–6, 8/4 if turn 7–8**. Tied first: only lower award to each tied player; no other award. Tied second receive none.

**Court/workshops:** If Company survived, add Court's current VP per Company share. If failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Scores may be negative.

**Final retirements/failure card:**

| Company outcome | Final retirement or failure step |
|---|---|
| Survived | Roll office attrition, then retire Pensioners; **no prestige/display cards**. |
| Failed | Instead draw **ONE RANDOM Company failure card** and resolve its printed consequence. |

Firm-track VP per share: Value 1 = −1 VP; 2 = 0; 3–4 = ½; 5–7 = 1; 8–9 = 1½; 10 = 2. The firm's Value number is also used for expenses; its VP rate is the symbol beneath that number.

Highest final VP wins. Ties: most windows, then clockwise from PM. Prizes, luxuries and spouse points are generally recorded when gained/lost, not added again at final scoring.

## Scoring / Victory Conditions

The game ends after scenario's final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Normally failure is immediate; failure during Events finishes that phase, and legislation failure finishes vote before scoring. Once game over, stop negotiations, calling promises and playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use. **During all of Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.**

**Final Scoring order — finish each row before the next:**

| Step | Procedure |
|---|---|
| 1. Firms, if deregulated | **BEFORE ordinary Power/Court/final-outcome scoring**, for each player separately add VP from all their shares across all their firms, then **round that player's total DOWN once**. Deduct **1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison**. **The next row (step2) describes the ONE eligible special firm retirement per shareholder, even on Company failure; ordinary scoring begins at step3.** |
| 2. Firm special retirement, if deregulated | Each eligible shareholder may retire **one member from supply**, after firm scoring but **BEFORE Power or any other ordinary final scoring**. Applies whether Company survived OR failed; no display cards. |
| 3. Power | Calculate Power and award its VP, as below. |
| 4. Court/workshops | Score Company shares and, on failure, uninvested workshops, as below. |
| 5. Final retirements OR failure card | Resolve the appropriate Company outcome below. Firm special retirement in step2 occurs in **either** outcome and is not replaced by the failure card. |

**Power award:** Count **enterprises and Company shares**, using their current Power-track rates (bottom two positions zero), +1 per passed-law token and trophy, +2 for PM, plus printed card power (blackmail faceup or down, applicable spouse). Most/second awards are **3/1 VP if final turn 1–3, 5/2 if turn 4–6, 8/4 if turn 7–8**. Tied first: only lower award to each tied player; no other award. Tied second receive none.

**Court/workshops:** If Company survived, add Court's current VP per Company share. If failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Scores may be negative.

**Final retirements/failure card:**

| Company outcome | Final retirement or failure step |
|---|---|
| Survived | Roll office attrition, then retire Pensioners; **no prestige/display cards**. |
| Failed | Instead draw **ONE RANDOM Company failure card** and resolve its printed consequence. |

### VII. Events in India (pp28–33)

**First roll the storm die:** a sea-zone result affects **that zone**, three storms affects **ALL sea zones**, and no storm indication means **NO storm checks**. The die face also specifies the **number of India events**. Resolve all required storms **before drawing any event**. Then flip and resolve **one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as the number printed on that die face**. Where an event uses a region, normally read the **back of the new top tile** in the draw stack, not the tile just drawn; follow each event's specific location rule.

**Storms:** Determine eligibility in the zone(s) specified above before rolling:

| Ships | Storm exposure |
|---|---|
| Company and extra ships | **Exempt**; never roll storm checks. |
| Player-owned ships in Company fleets | Check ships in the affected sea zone(s). |
| Ships assigned to China | Count as **Eastern** sea zone. |
| Firm ships | Count in the sea zone on their **firm strategy**, even though on a charter. |
| Hobnob firm ships | **Exempt** from storms. |

Roll **once per eligible ship**: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Return a sunk ship to its shipyard **unfatigued**.

**Closing orders and Cascades:** Return any writer on a newly closed order to its owner's supply; flip a filled token to closed. If told to close an order in an already fully closed region, Cascade: close all open orders directly connected to that region's orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region's northernmost open order instead. If none are open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate a Cascade only once per event tile but can receive multiple Cascades' effects.

| Event | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Turmoil | Close northernmost open order in top-stack region; if all closed, Cascade. |
| Windfall | Owners take £1 per writer on orders in top-stack region and every bordering region. |
| Shuffle | Elephant's March, then shuffle this tile with remaining draw stack; separately shuffle discards and place on top. If draw stack empty, March last instead. |
| Leader | Top-stack sovereign region gains one tower. Dominated region instead rebels with printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled. |
| Peace | Open orders connected across Elephant's border and add one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant wholly inside a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March. |
| Crisis | Resolve at Elephant's location, tail attacking head, then March. Use procedures below. |
| Foreign Invasion | Roll storm die for target regions: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal; all storms means each, none means top-stack region. Per target roll ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack. On success close all orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target's flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. |

**Choose the ordinary Crisis procedure from the Elephant:** Its **tail is the attacker/acting region; its head is the defender**. A sovereign actor (large capital flag or unflagged dome) causes **Invasion**. A dominated actor (small flag or no dome) causes **Rebellion against its sovereign**. If Elephant is wholly inside a Company region, resolve Rebellion against the Company. This classifier concerns ordinary Elephant-located Crisis events; Foreign Invasion uses its own location rule.

**Invasion Crisis:** Sovereign attacker's whole empire strength + event modifier must be **greater than** defender's whole empire strength. On success, replace defender's flag with attacker's dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its entire empire. If attacker had no empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none available no new empire/flags form. On failure, attacker loses one tower.

**Rebellion Crisis:** Compare only rebelling region strength + modifier against its sovereign capital's strength; other empire regions do not count. Must be strictly greater. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed). Failure removes one tower from the capital.

**Attacks on Company:** An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve attacks in this order: **primary Crisis first**, then secondary regions in **Bombay → Madras → Bengal** Army order. **Within each Presidency, that Commander chooses the order of its associated regions.** Attack strengths are distinct:

- **Primary normal Crisis:** normal Invasion/Rebellion attack strength **plus unrest in its target region**.
- **Primary Foreign Invasion:** the ordinary attack die, with no added unrest (designer ruling in FAQ).
- **Every secondary Rebellion:** **only the number of unrest cubes in that secondary region**; no event modifier or empire strength.

**Mounting defense — first identify who acts:**

| Defense office situation | Acting player |
|---|---|
| Associated Commander occupied | That Commander chooses and exhausts pieces; normal trophy gains/losses apply. |
| Commander vacant | **Military Affairs itself acts in the Commander's stead**, choosing pieces; gains/loses **no trophies**. |
| Commander AND Military Affairs vacant | **Chairman chooses pieces** and gains/loses **no trophies**. |

This is acting for the defense, **not appointing a new Commander**. The acting player exhausts active Army pieces to reach at least the Crisis strength, or as many as possible if unable to reach it. Local alliances provide printed strength usable once; **their strength cannot be split among more than one purpose**. The following strength comparison applies the **user-supplied interpretation** recorded under Special Rules & Edge Cases:

| Total strength of newly exhausted pieces | Attack and defense result |
|---|---|
| **EQUAL TO OR GREATER THAN** Crisis strength | **The attack FAILS; defense SUCCEEDS.** Remove all unrest in the attacked region. The **actual Commander gains one trophy**; **Military Affairs/Chairman substitutes gain OR lose NO trophies**. If this defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible. |
| **LESS THAN** Crisis strength | **The attack SUCCEEDS; defense FAILS.** Perform Region Loss. If the successful primary Crisis was an Invasion, apply empire creation/growth. |

**Example:** Exhausting an active strength-2 local alliance successfully defends a strength-1 Crisis. Exhaust the whole alliance piece; its excess strength does not cause the defense to fail.

**Region Loss:** Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up, then Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in associated Army: each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate Governor: return office card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies. Remove Governor overlay, partially built Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion's specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to its region with **the £ loot side DOWN and the region-symbol side UP**. Future conquest gets no loot modifier; region loses its Presidency association. An Invasion Crisis closes all its orders, or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals number of regions lost **so far this turn**, including this one: first -1, second additional -2, etc. If this causes failure, finish Events in India before Final Scoring. **Losing one region does not automatically lose any other Company region: resolve each other attack and its defense separately.**

**Elephant's March:** After successful Invasion Crisis, move to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise top-stack region. Company region: place fully inside. Dominated region: point toward its sovereign. Sovereign: point across shape-marked border on tile. If that neighbor is already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor that is not. If all neighbors dominated, use the redirect-arrow shape's border, pointing toward empire capital.

## FAQ & Rulings

**Company Fraud payout cap:** The player receives only the cash actually removed from Company Balance. For example, Balance £10 and highest roll 6 results in Balance £0 and a £10 payout, not £12. Cole Wehrle confirmed that exact alternative on September 24, 2022. [Designer ruling](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2938749/article/40850873#40850873). Use the corrected card timing: start of Revenue.

**Foreign Invasion and unrest:** Cole Wehrle clarified on April 30, 2023 that unrest does **not** add to a Foreign Invasion's primary attack strength or determine its resulting tower levels. Use the ordinary die roll for attack strength; after a successful Foreign Invasion, set towers to **half that roll, rounded down**. The event still uses the Company-defense procedure and its secondary unrest attacks. Do not apply the normal primary Crisis's added unrest to this special event. [Designer ruling](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2962161/article/42192767#42192767). **On a successful Foreign Invasion, close all orders in the target region once; if they are already all closed, Cascade instead.** Region Loss does not close them a second time: its additional closure is only for a normal Invasion Crisis.

**Applicable official errata:** The publisher links the [official errata discussion](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2936700/official-errata), whose original designer post links the full internal correction list. The assigned Second Printing rulebook incorporates the core procedural corrections, including forced prize-piece reuse, empty Court, deployment boundaries, Region Loss and Elephant priority. Corrected setup cards supply Bengal's 1758 control token and 1813 control/share-value tokens. Printed card corrections also specify: Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reducing a check to zero dice means failure; Company Fraud is played at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take cash from the bank equal to that actual Balance reduction; Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies; Military Oversight demotes one Commander to an officer, then appoints a Commander from officers: **the SAME former Commander remains eligible to become COMMANDER again**. **Attrition:** Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Pay its printed cost, move the member to the prize and gain printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display-selection order, then pay bank. |---|---|
| Company and extra ships | **Exempt**; never roll storm checks. |
| Player-owned ships in Company fleets | Check ships in the affected sea zone(s). |
| Ships assigned to China | Count as **Eastern** sea zone. |
| Firm ships | Count in the sea zone on their **firm strategy**, even though on a charter. |
| Hobnob firm ships | **Exempt** from storms. |

|---|---|
| Turmoil | Close northernmost open order in top-stack region; if all closed, Cascade. |
| Windfall | Owners take £1 per writer on orders in top-stack region and every bordering region. |
| Shuffle | Elephant's March, then shuffle this tile with remaining draw stack; separately shuffle discards and place on top. If draw stack empty, March last instead. |
| Leader | Top-stack sovereign region gains one tower. Dominated region instead rebels with printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled. |
| Peace | Open orders connected across Elephant's border and add one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant wholly inside a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March. |
| Crisis | Resolve at Elephant's location, tail attacking head, then March. Use procedures below. |
| Foreign Invasion | Roll storm die for target regions: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal; all storms means each, none means top-stack region. Per target roll ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack. On success close all orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target's flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half attack roll rounded down. If Elephant is wholly inside a Company region, resolve Rebellion against the Company. This classifier concerns ordinary Elephant-located Crisis events; Foreign Invasion uses its own location rule.

**Invasion Crisis:** Sovereign attacker's whole empire strength + event modifier must be **greater than** defender's whole empire strength. On success, replace defender's flag with attacker's dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its entire empire. | Defense office situation | Acting player |
|---|---|
| Associated Commander occupied | That Commander chooses and exhausts pieces; normal trophy gains/losses apply. |
| Commander vacant | **Military Affairs itself acts in the Commander's stead**, choosing pieces; gains/loses **no trophies**. |
| Commander AND Military Affairs vacant | **Chairman chooses pieces** and gains/loses **no trophies**. |

Local alliances provide printed strength usable once; **their strength cannot be split among more than one purpose**. The following strength comparison applies the **user-supplied interpretation** recorded under Special Rules & Edge Cases:

| Total strength of newly exhausted pieces | Attack and defense result |
|---|---|
| **EQUAL TO OR GREATER THAN** Crisis strength | **The attack FAILS; defense SUCCEEDS.** Remove all unrest in the attacked region. The **actual Commander gains one trophy**; **Military Affairs/Chairman substitutes gain OR lose NO trophies**. If this defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible. |

Eliminate Governor: return office card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies. Remove Governor overlay, partially built Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion's specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to its region with **the £ loot side DOWN and the region-symbol side UP**. Future conquest gets no loot modifier; region loses its Presidency association. An Invasion Crisis closes all its orders, or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals number of regions lost **so far this turn**, including this one: first -1, second additional -2, etc. If this causes failure, finish Events in India before Final Scoring. **Losing one region does not automatically lose any other Company region: resolve each other attack and its defense separately.**

**Elephant's March:** After successful Invasion Crisis, move to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise top-stack region. Company region: place fully inside. Dominated region: point toward its sovereign. Sovereign: point across shape-marked border on tile. If that neighbor is already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor that is not. If all neighbors dominated, use the redirect-arrow shape's border, pointing toward empire capital.

<!-- qa-unit:T168:end -->

## Scoring / Victory Conditions

The game ends after scenario's final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Normally failure is immediate; failure during Events finishes that phase, and legislation failure finishes vote before scoring. Once game over, stop negotiations, calling promises and playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use. **During all of Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.**

**Final Scoring order — finish each row before the next:**

| Step | Procedure |
|---|---|
| 1. Firms, if deregulated | **BEFORE ordinary Power/Court/final-outcome scoring**, for each player separately add VP from all their shares across all their firms, then **round that player's total DOWN once**. Deduct **1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison**. **The next row (step2) describes the ONE eligible special firm retirement per shareholder, even on Company failure; ordinary scoring begins at step3.** |
| 2. Firm special retirement, if deregulated | Each eligible shareholder may retire **one member from supply**, after firm scoring but **BEFORE Power or any other ordinary final scoring**. Applies whether Company survived OR failed; no display cards. |
| 3. Power | Calculate Power and award its VP, as below. |
| 4. Court/workshops | Score Company shares and, on failure, uninvested workshops, as below. |
| 5. Final retirements OR failure card | Resolve the appropriate Company outcome below. Firm special retirement in step2 occurs in **either** outcome and is not replaced by the failure card. |

**Power award:** Count **enterprises and Company shares**, using their current Power-track rates (bottom two positions zero), +1 per passed-law token and trophy, +2 for PM, plus printed card power (blackmail faceup or down, applicable spouse). Most/second awards are **3/1 VP if final turn 1–3, 5/2 if turn 4–6, 8/4 if turn 7–8**. Tied first: only lower award to each tied player; no other award. Tied second receive none.

**Court/workshops:** If Company survived, add Court's current VP per Company share. If failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Scores may be negative.

**Final retirements/failure card:**

| Company outcome | Final retirement or failure step |
|---|---|
| Survived | Roll office attrition, then retire Pensioners; **no prestige/display cards**. |
| Failed | Instead draw **ONE RANDOM Company failure card** and resolve its printed consequence. |

Firm-track VP per share: Value 1 = −1 VP; 2 = 0; 3–4 = ½; 5–7 = 1; 8–9 = 1½; 10 = 2. The firm's Value number is also used for expenses; its VP rate is the symbol beneath that number.

Highest final VP wins. Ties: most windows, then clockwise from PM. Prizes, luxuries and spouse points are generally recorded when gained/lost, not added again at final scoring.

### VII. Events in India (pp28–33)

**First roll the storm die:** a sea-zone result affects **that zone**, three storms affects **ALL sea zones**, and no storm indication means **NO storm checks**. The die face also specifies the **number of India events**. Resolve all required storms **before drawing any event**. Then flip and resolve **one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as the number printed on that die face**. Where an event uses a region, normally read the **back of the new top tile** in the draw stack, not the tile just drawn; follow each event's specific location rule.

**Storms:** Determine eligibility in the zone(s) specified above before rolling:

| Ships | Storm exposure |
|---|---|
| Company and extra ships | **Exempt**; never roll storm checks. |
| Player-owned ships in Company fleets | Check ships in the affected sea zone(s). |
| Ships assigned to China | Count as **Eastern** sea zone. |
| Firm ships | Count in the sea zone on their **firm strategy**, even though on a charter. |
| Hobnob firm ships | **Exempt** from storms. |

Roll **once per eligible ship**: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Return a sunk ship to its shipyard **unfatigued**.

**Closing orders and Cascades:** Return any writer on a newly closed order to its owner's supply; flip a filled token to closed. If told to close an order in an already fully closed region, Cascade: close all open orders directly connected to that region's orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region's northernmost open order instead. If none are open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate a Cascade only once per event tile but can receive multiple Cascades' effects.

| Event | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Turmoil | Close northernmost open order in top-stack region; if all closed, Cascade. |
| Windfall | Owners take £1 per writer on orders in top-stack region and every bordering region. |
| Shuffle | Elephant's March, then shuffle this tile with remaining draw stack; separately shuffle discards and place on top. If draw stack empty, March last instead. |
| Leader | Top-stack sovereign region gains one tower. Dominated region instead rebels with printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled. |
| Peace | Open orders connected across Elephant's border and add one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant wholly inside a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March. |
| Crisis | Resolve at Elephant's location, tail attacking head, then March. Use procedures below. |
| Foreign Invasion | Roll storm die for target regions: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal; all storms means each, none means top-stack region. Per target roll ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack. On success close all orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target's flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. |

**Choose the ordinary Crisis procedure from the Elephant:** Its **tail is the attacker/acting region; its head is the defender**. A sovereign actor (large capital flag or unflagged dome) causes **Invasion**. A dominated actor (small flag or no dome) causes **Rebellion against its sovereign**. If Elephant is wholly inside a Company region, resolve Rebellion against the Company. This classifier concerns ordinary Elephant-located Crisis events; Foreign Invasion uses its own location rule.

**Invasion Crisis:** Sovereign attacker's whole empire strength + event modifier must be **greater than** defender's whole empire strength. On success, replace defender's flag with attacker's dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its entire empire. If attacker had no empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none available no new empire/flags form. On failure, attacker loses one tower.

**Rebellion Crisis:** Compare only rebelling region strength + modifier against its sovereign capital's strength; other empire regions do not count. Must be strictly greater. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed). Failure removes one tower from the capital.

**Attacks on Company:** An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve attacks in this order: **primary Crisis first**, then secondary regions in **Bombay → Madras → Bengal** Army order. **Within each Presidency, that Commander chooses the order of its associated regions.** Attack strengths are distinct:

- **Primary normal Crisis:** normal Invasion/Rebellion attack strength **plus unrest in its target region**.
- **Primary Foreign Invasion:** the ordinary attack die, with no added unrest (designer ruling in FAQ).
- **Every secondary Rebellion:** **only the number of unrest cubes in that secondary region**; no event modifier or empire strength.

| Defense office situation | Acting player |
|---|---|
| Associated Commander occupied | That Commander chooses and exhausts pieces; normal trophy gains/losses apply. |
| Commander vacant | **Military Affairs itself acts in the Commander's stead**, choosing pieces; gains/loses **no trophies**. |
| Commander AND Military Affairs vacant | **Chairman chooses pieces** and gains/loses **no trophies**. |

This is acting for the defense, **not appointing a new Commander**. The acting player exhausts active Army pieces to reach at least the Crisis strength, or as many as possible if unable to reach it. Local alliances provide printed strength usable once; **their strength cannot be split among more than one purpose**. The following strength comparison applies the **user-supplied interpretation** recorded under Special Rules & Edge Cases:

| Total strength of newly exhausted pieces | Attack and defense result |
|---|---|
| **EQUAL TO OR GREATER THAN** Crisis strength | **The attack FAILS; defense SUCCEEDS.** Remove all unrest in the attacked region.
